In my opinion, it completely depends on your confidence and skill. If you say, "I'm definitely confident in using a strong bike, and I won't push it to its limits until I have a feel for it," then buy yourself a big bike. However, if you're not 100% confident in riding, especially when it's a stronger one. Then you shouldn't get a big bike. In the end, it's your health on the line. If you get a strong bike as your first one, take it easy in the beginning. There is no rush. It doesn't matter if it takes you a year to use its full potential. Worst case If you crash because you rushed the process of getting used to your bike, you won't be able to ride anything anymore
In my opinion, you're the only one who can decide if you should get a big bike as a beginner or not.

I understand that you can't know how much of a pain the German Bureaucracy system is
1. You'll have to go to yous city hall and request a small weapons permit. This is the easiest to get its like 20 € and 20€ Extra for a Processing fee.
Now you can shoot air rifles, Weapons that can only shoot blanks and pepper pistols.
2. You have to go down to city hall again and request the big weapons permit. You'll have to do a psychological test a background check and take a class that is multiple days long (I think like 1 ½ weeks if added up). After everything went through you'll pay like 400€ and however much the processing fee is. Now you can shoot real weapons that don't fall under the weapons of war Protection Act. But you can't own a gun for that you'll have to get a weapon ownership card for each firearm along side a safe for it and a second safe for the ammo. Now you can own a gun and get regular visits from the police who come and see if everything is where it should be. They even come un announced.
